rationale: B wins because it turns the same raw facts into sharper, safer pitch choices and is more honest about what is not ready. Its best move is "Why a business would hold a stablecoin balance to pay suppliers abroad" because it adds the missing ground-level customer story and correctly marks it as second-wave. A is solid, but "For a profitable public payments company, cutting correspondent-banking fees is a margin story" overstates the margin implication before Wise has given cost or volume migration data. B gives the founder a usable pitching order; A gives four good rooms to walk into, then forgets to say which door is actually unlocked.
gaps_in_A: "For a profitable public payments company, cutting correspondent-banking fees is a margin story" asserts the economics too hard. The update says transfers are faster and cheaper than correspondent banking, not that Wise's own margins improve.
"One of the biggest cross-border payment networks" is plausible from £30B per quarter, but the update does not establish market rank. Big claim, thin footing.
The set misses a kept customer/treasury angle. It notices the hole in "No named business customer or case study appears," but leaves a useful second-wave story on the floor.
"journalist-fit-check — four viable journalist shapes exist" is too eager. At least the regulatory and category angles need the stablecoin, partner, and first markets before names are worth pulling.
gaps_in_B: "turns its launch sequence into a public map of which regulators are ready" is a smart frame, but it risks outrunning the facts until the first live markets and approval basis are named.
"direct challenge to those banks' revenue line" is directionally reasonable, but still inferred. It needs bank-fee exposure or analyst comment before becoming copy, not just angle logic.

"Which stablecoin did Wise pick?" is labeled `hallucinated_fact`, but the question itself is not a hallucination. The real problem is that it is an under-reported fact gap, not a standalone owned angle.
"the first-market decision is the news" assumes there is a first-market decision available. The set later catches this, but the angle headline should carry that conditionality more cleanly.
